key_insight: An optimizer that learns faster during pretraining does not necessarily produce better results after fine-tuning. With enough pretraining data, AdamW overtakes Muon in downstream performance.
problem_solved: Tests whether Muon's advantage in reducing pretraining loss translates into better downstream performance after fine-tuning.
method: Compare downstream fine-tuning outcomes for models pretrained with Muon versus AdamW.
Vary pretraining data budgets to identify when the performance ranking reverses.
Examine how model size affects the optimizer comparison.
impact: Practitioners should evaluate optimizers using post-fine-tuning performance, not pretraining loss alone. Optimizer choice may depend on the pretraining data budget and model size.
visual_elements: Conceptual crossover chart: downstream performance versus pretraining data budget, with AdamW overtaking Muon.
Two-stage pipeline: pretraining optimizer choice → fine-tuning → downstream evaluation.
Side-by-side panels contrasting Muon's pretraining-loss advantage with AdamW's fine-tuning advantage at larger data budgets.
Model-size icons highlighting scale as another variable in optimizer selection.
paper_title: Pretraining Data Scale Reverses the Muon-AdamW Fine-Tuning Gap
paper_authors: Catherine Li, Jingchu Gai, Andrej Risteski, Jacob Mitchell Springer, Aditi Raghunathan
